names.summary: A 72-byte housekeeping beacon with a unix-time clock, a solar input, two battery-related voltages, a group of four temperatures, a rolling counter, and a few slowly varying orbit-phase fields. All frames fall within 80 minutes of an eclipse, so the lag correlations are real recovery physics.

fields.name: unix_timestamp
fields.rationale: u4le increases at 1.0 s/s with zero resets and the values are consistent with a unix epoch (about 1.79e9). [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_current
fields.rationale: Exactly zero in shadow and about 200 in sun (rho_sun 0.93). The hint is power_solar and the field is rough. The unit is a guess. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_cell_voltage
fields.rationale: 4020-4141 is in the single Li-ion cell range (3000-4200 mV). The spread is narrow, it is higher in sun, and it moves with offsets 29 and 57. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_pack_voltage
fields.rationale: 8118-8306 is roughly twice the value at offset 27, which suggests a two-cell pack. It is charged by sunlight and has a narrow spread. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: internal_temp_a
fields.rationale: It is a small value of 0-18 that follows the orbital phase (r2 0.2) and does not respond to sun versus shadow. It moves with offsets 34 and 68, but the physical quantity is unclear. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: internal_temp_b
fields.rationale: It is nearly identical in behaviour and range to offset 33, so it is likely a sibling sensor. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_1
fields.rationale: A signed byte that is about +20 in sun and -3 in shadow. It falls in shadow (trend -0.52) and the four panels move together. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_2
fields.rationale: Same sun/shadow swing and shadow trend as the other panel temperatures. It is a signed byte in a plausible degC range. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_3
fields.rationale: Largest swing of the group (+22 in sun, -6 in shadow) with a strong negative trend in shadow, typical of an outer panel. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: panel_temp_4
fields.rationale: Follows sunlight with a tau of 5-80 min, with the same behaviour as the other three panel temperatures. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_voltage_secondary
fields.rationale: Range of 8000-8340 is similar to offset 29 and it moves with offsets 27 and 29. It is higher in sun but coarser, with only 10 distinct values. It is probably a second pack-voltage measurement. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: sequence_counter
fields.rationale: A 1-byte counter that rises at 0.1/s and wraps at 255. The wraps are by design, not reboots. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: internal_temp_c
fields.rationale: It has the same orbital behaviour as offsets 33 and 34, with a small spread and no sun/shadow step. The power_battery hint is not convincing because it is flat between sun and shadow. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: Not much evidence of trouble: the clock has no resets and the counter wraps are by design. Battery voltages are in a normal Li-ion range and recover in sunlight. The apparent rise in the daily low of the voltages is probably a seasonal or sampling effect over 21 days, so ageing cannot be judged.

names.summary: 72-byte beacon, apparently a navigation/ADCS-type frame. It holds a 3-byte rolling counter, float32 state vectors (ECI position and velocity), a unit quaternion and a few orbit-phase-dependent values. Several fields that look like power or sun correlates are really orbit-geometry artefacts.

fields.name: frame_counter
fields.rationale: Monotonic u3 counter, 20 wraps within passes and 24 resets in the window. The rate is 0.018/s, so it is probably a sub-sampled or free-running tick counter, not a simple sequence number. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: orbit_phase_byte
fields.rationale: u1 varies with orbital phase (r2 0.445) but has no sun physics. It may be a position-related byte or part of a neighbouring float. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: eclipse_flag_byte
fields.rationale: Two-level step (-54 in sun, 74 in shadow) with 5 distinct values and no trend, so it acts as an eclipse flag. It moves with offsets 18 and 34, which are float fields. It is probably the unaligned byte of a neighbouring float, not a battery signal, despite the power_battery hint. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: position_eci_y
fields.scale: raw / 1009.685 km (about raw*0.001 km if metres)
fields.rationale: Linear in the ECI y coordinate (raw_per_km about 1000 = metres), but only 34% of frames match, so there are stale or no-fix values. The power_battery hint is spurious and results from orbit geometry. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: position_eci_z_or_x
fields.rationale: Float with magnitude up to 6.4e6, which is Earth-radius scale in metres, and a strong orbital-phase dependence. It is likely another position component, so it is not a power field. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: velocity_or_position_component
fields.rationale: Orbit-periodic float, magnitude about 6000. It moves with offset 22, so it could be a velocity or position component, but the frame is unaligned and a huge max value suggests misaligned bytes. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: velocity_eci_y
fields.rationale: Matches ECI y velocity at about 1000 raw per km/s, so it is in m/s. Only 36% of frames agree, which suggests stale fixes. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: velocity_component_x_or_z
fields.rationale: Float of magnitude up to 7.6e3, comparable to orbital speed in m/s, and orbit-periodic with a sun-like sign change. It is probably another ECI velocity component, not a battery field. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: attitude_quaternion
fields.rationale: Four consecutive floats with unit norm in 99.7% of frames, i.e. a quaternion. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: Not enough evidence. The counter shows 24 resets in the window, the latest 0.5 days before the end, which suggests reboots or a rolling counter that wraps by design. No reliable battery or thermal fields were identified.
